observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: 0x004adb44 MOV dword ptr [EBP-0x4],ECX spills ECX and 0x004adb47 MOV EAX,dword ptr [EBP-0x4] reloads it into the address register, so ECX is the receiver. No instruction in the body reads any stack slot, and 0x004adb50 RET carries no immediate, so there is no stack argument and no callee cleanup. That is exactly the __thiscall machine shape with zero parameters. Ghidra's decompilation labels it __fastcall, which is a labelling artefact of the applied prototype, not a machine fact: EDX is never read.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: The exact 32-bit pattern stored at receiver+0x44, widened to a float and left in x87 register ST(0). No conversion, no normalisation, no scaling and no default.
observed_original_abi.return_register: ST(0) (the x87 register stack, not a GPR)
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x004adb4a FLD float ptr [EAX + 0x44] performs a 4-byte memory load and pushes exactly one x87 register. 0x004adb4d MOV ESP,EBP and 0x004adb4f POP EBP unwind the integer frame without touching the x87 stack, so the loaded value survives the epilogue in ST(0). Every sampled call site consumes it with an immediate FSTP or FCOMIP and none reads EAX afterwards.
observed_original_abi.stack_cleanup_owner: not applicable; there is no stack argument
observed_original_abi.frame: PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / PUSH ECX / MOV [EBP-4],ECX / ... / MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP. The PUSH ECX and the spill at 0x004adb44 are dead: no instruction other than the reload at 0x004adb47 reads EBP-0x4. This is the same shape as the ten sibling accessors in the 0x004adaa0..0x004adc40 range, all of which carry the identical redundant spill.
observed_original_abi.receiver_note: The receiver is a sub-object, not the rigblock itself. Two proven provenances: cEditor+0x98 at 0x00586f05, and a stack-loaded local at 0x0049ad18. 0x00438700 independently shows that the +0x4c..+0x4f flag block of the same sub-object is reached as a rigblock's +0x28 member. No vtable was located for this sub-object, so no owning class is named.

semantic_contract: Given any receiver R for which R+0x44 is readable, the function returns the exact 32-bit pattern stored at R+0x44 widened to a float, in ST(0), and leaves the rest of the receiver untouched. Because the load is a single 4-byte FLD there is no normalisation: every one of the 2^32 stored bit patterns, including negative zero, denormals, infinities and signalling NaN payloads, is returned unchanged. The function pushes exactly one x87 register net, so the caller's x87 stack must have room and must consume the value. It is pure, idempotent and re-entrant, with no call, no allocation, no global access and no write of any kind. A null receiver is not checked and faults. The value is never interpreted at this site, so the contract is 'return the stored bits'; the only place a meaning is visible is 0x00586f10 in cEditor::SetEditorModel, where the field is compared against a computed float and a JBE branches on the result, which makes it behave as a threshold. The receiver is a sub-object rather than the rigblock: cEditor+0x98 and a rigblock's +0x28 are both proven provenances, and the neighbouring +0x4c..+0x4f bytes form a four-flag block on that same sub-object.
classification_rationale: The complete body is nine instructions and every one of them was read directly; the field offset and width are proven by the single FLD, the ABI is proven by the bare RET and the dead spill, and the return form is corroborated by ten sibling accessors in one contiguous disassembly window and by four call sites that immediately FSTP or FCOMIP the result. The behavioural contract -- return the stored 32-bit pattern in ST(0), pure, no guard -- is therefore established, not merely the layout. The one material element that stays bounded is the identity and meaning of the field: the receiver has two different proven provenances that do not converge on a named type, no vtable was located for it, and the single site that interprets the value only shows it being used as a comparison operand, which is consistent with a distance, a scale or a threshold without distinguishing them. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld for that reason and not for the body. STRUCTURAL_ONLY would understate the evidence, since a behavioural claim is made and is fully read from the binary.
semantic_findings: The function is a pure field read. The PUSH ECX / MOV [EBP-4],ECX / MOV EAX,[EBP-4] sequence is a redundant spill and reload that no other instruction consumes; the observable body is the single FLD.
The return is a 4-byte float in ST(0), not in EAX. Every sampled call site consumes it with an immediate FSTP or FCOMIP, and none reads EAX afterwards.

The value is never interpreted at this site, so the contract is 'return the stored bits'. The one place a meaning is visible is 0x00586f10, where the field is compared against a computed float and a JBE branches on the result.

The receiver is reached through at least two different owner members: cEditor+0x98 at 0x00586f05 and a stack-loaded local at 0x0049ad18. Combined with 0x00438700 calling the +0x4f sibling 0x004adc40 on a rigblock's +0x28 sub-object, this shows the +0x38..+0x4f block belongs to a sub-object and not to the rigblock itself.

The sibling accessor family is dense and contiguous: 0x004adaa0 (+0x38), 0x004adb00 (+0x40), this function (+0x44), 0x004adc00 (+0x48 setter), 0x004adba0 / 0x004adb80 (+0x4c), 0x004adbe0 / 0x004adbc0 (+0x4d), 0x004adb60 (+0x4e setter), 0x004adc20 / 0x004adc40 (+0x4f). Every one of them was disassembled in this batch, so the float run at +0x38 / +0x40 / +0x44 / +0x48 and the four flag bytes at +0x4c..+0x4f are established as a group. The accessors are asymmetric: +0x48 and +0x4e have setters only.

The +0x38, +0x40 and +0x44 floats are passed together to the same call at 0x0049ad1e-0x0049ad3c, twice in FUN_0049a2a0. Three consecutive floats consumed as one argument group is a layout fact about the group, independent of what the group means.

0x00448e90 reads +0x48, +0x4c and +0x50 of a rigblock as three dwords with the top bit of +0x48 flipped by XOR 0x80000000, i.e. as a packed position. That is a different object from this one, because +0x48 is a float here and a packed word there. The two layouts must not be merged.
clang++ 22.1.8 -m32 -O2 emits `flds 0x44(%ecx) ; ret` for the reconstruction: 3 bytes against the original's 17, same load width, same receiver register, same return register, bare ret.
unresolved_questions: What does the float at +0x44 mean? The only site that gives it a role compares it against a computed float, which is consistent with a distance, a scale or a threshold. None of those is asserted.
What class owns this sub-object? Its proven parent contexts are cEditor+0x98 and rigblock+0x28, and no vtable was located for it.
Why does the float run start at +0x38? The float at +0x3c has no accessor in the 0x004adaa0..0x004adc40 range, so either it is accessed elsewhere or the run is not contiguous. Not resolved.
Is +0x40 / +0x44 / +0x48 a vector, a bound or a centre? Three consecutive floats exist and are read together at 0x0049ad1e-0x0049ad3c, which is suggestive but does not fix the axes or the order.
Why do +0x48 and +0x4e have setters but no getters in this family? Either they are read by inlined code elsewhere or the getters were never emitted out of line. Not resolved.

Is the PUSH ECX / spill / reload sequence in all ten family members an artefact of a debug build, a /Zi-style build, or a compiler that emits frames for trivially small functions? Nothing in the observed evidence distinguishes these, and it does not affect semantics.
Seven of the eleven reported call sites were not disassembled window-by-window in this batch; their receiver provenances come from the briefing's call graph.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists, so the claim that the field holds a live float in the shipping build is static only.
A runtime pass would need to sample the field at a known call site, for example around 0x00586f10, to see the value the original actually compares against.
The original Cell stage has never been entered in any recorded run, so no stage-level reachability claim is made.
